# Data

## Read, Format, & Sample

```{r}
# read in data
raw <- read.csv("Metro_mlp_uc_sfrcondo_month.csv")
raw <- raw[-1,]  # get rid of labels row
# pivoted
raw <- raw |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -(1:5),
    names_to = "Date",
    values_to = "Value")
# make date a date obj
raw <- raw |> 
  mutate(Date = ymd(substring(Date, first = 2))) |> 
  mutate(Time = yearmonth(Date))

# select some regions with no gaps
sampNoGaps <- raw |> 
  filter(RegionName %in% c(
        "New York, NY", "Detroit, MI", "Dallas, TX", 
        "Denver, CO", "Los Angeles, CA"
      ))
# put into a time series object
ts5 <- sampNoGaps |> 
  dplyr::select(-c(1, 2, 4, 5)) |> 
  tsibble(key = RegionName, index = Time)

# train/test split
train5 <- ts5 |>  # 300 obs
  filter(Time < yearmonth("2024 January")) |> 
  dplyr::select(-Date)  # don't want to accidentally use
test5 <- ts5 |>  # 225 obs
  filter(Time >= yearmonth("2024 January")) |> 
  dplyr::select(-Date)  # don't want to accidentally use
```

# Model Each Region Separately

```{r}
# create cross-validation training set
cv_horizon <- 12  # how many steps to forecast for each fold
cv_step <- 12  # how many obs to add to the next fold
end_of_first_fold <- yearmonth("2021 Jan")  # date that the first fold ends 
train5_cv <- train5 |>
  stretch_tsibble(
    .init = 36,  # number of months where the *first* fold ends (= 1st 2 cycles)
                 # -> Jan 2021 = 36 months from Jan 2018 (first obs)
    .step = cv_step) |>  # each later fold adds 12 months
  filter(# last month of train data is Dec 2023, and we only keep folds with a 
         # CV forecast horizon inside the train data (which ends at 72 months)
    .id <= 3)  # folds with forecasts inside train set

# create empty list to store each region's top model
top_region_models <- c()


# function that fits chosen models on the data passed
fit_candidates <- function(data){
  data |> model(  # fit the 16 potential models
    # ETS ----
    `ETS(M,A,A)`  = ETS(Value ~ error("M") + trend("A") + season("A")),
    `ETS(M,A,M)`  = ETS(Value ~ error("M") + trend("A") + season("M")),
    `ETS(A,A,M)`  = ETS(Value ~ error("A") + trend("A") + season("M")),
    `ETS(A,Ad,M)` = ETS(Value ~ error("A") + trend("Ad") + season("M")),
    `ETS(A,A,A)`  = ETS(Value ~ error("A") + trend("Ad") + season("A")),
    `ETS(A,Ad,A)` = ETS(Value ~ error("A") + trend("Ad") + season("A")),
    `ETS(M,Ad,M)` = ETS(Value ~ error("M") + trend("Ad") + season("M")),
    # >> 7 ETS models

    # DECOMPOSED ----
    `STL(annual) + NAIVE` = decomposition_model(
          STL(Value ~ trend() + season(period = 12), robust = TRUE), 
          NAIVE(season_adjust)),
    `STL(annual, no trend) + ETS(A,Ad,N)` = decomposition_model(
          STL(Value ~ season(period = 12), robust = TRUE), 
          ETS(season_adjust ~ error("A") + trend("Ad") + season("N"))),
    `STL(annual, no trend) + ETS(M,Ad,N)` = decomposition_model(
          STL(Value ~ season(period = 12), robust = TRUE), 
          ETS(season_adjust ~ error("M") + trend("Ad") + season("N"))),
    `STL(annual, no trend) + ARIMA(auto)` = decomposition_model(
          STL(Value ~ season(period = 12), robust = TRUE),
          ARIMA(season_adjust)),
    # >> 4 decomposition models

    # ARIMA ----
    `ARIMA(auto)` = ARIMA(Value),
    # >> 1 ARIMA model
    
    # BENCHMARK ----
    `Mean (benchmark)`           = MEAN(Value),
    `Naïve (benchmark)`          = NAIVE(Value),
    `Seasonal Naïve (benchmark)` = SNAIVE(Value ~ lag("1 year")),
    `Drift (benchmark)`          = RW(Value ~ drift())
    # >> 4 benchmark models
  )
}


# STEP 1 : fit models to an individual region using cross-validation
regionCV <- function(region){
  
  # TRAINING SETS ----
  # *cross-validation* training set for <region>
  region_train_cv <- train5_cv |>  # cv set (with folds)
    filter(RegionName == region) |> 
    dplyr::select(-1)  # remove RegionName column
  # *original* training set for <region>
  region_train <- train5 |>  # original time series (no folds)
    filter(RegionName == region) |> 
    dplyr::select(-1)  # remove RegionName column
  
  # PART 1 : fit models ----
  # apply time series cross-validation to training set
  region_cv_fits <- region_train_cv |>
    fit_candidates() |>  # fit all potential models
    forecast(h = cv_horizon)  # forecast each fold
  
  # PARTS 2 & 3 : diagnostics & model comparison ----
  # get accuracy measures for models across each fold
  cv_origin <- region_cv_fits |>  # (one row per model per fold)
    accuracy(region_train,  # use original training set (not CV set) for comparison
             by = c(".model", ".id")) |>  # scales each fold's MASE by that fold's own training data
    mutate(origin = end_of_first_fold + cv_step * (.id - 1))
  
  # > Measure 1 : How often is each model the best at a forecast origin?
  wins <- cv_origin |>  
    group_by(.id) |>  # group by fold
    slice_min(MASE, n = 1,  # select the model with the smallest MASE
              with_ties = TRUE) |>  # ties kept together (n may be > 1)
    ungroup() |>  # ungroup by fold
    count(.model,  # count times each model had smallest MASE (across all folds)
          name = "origins_won")
  
  wins_and_measures <- cv_origin |>
    group_by(.model) |>  # group by model
    summarize(cv_MASE = mean(MASE),  # get MASE for each model (all folds)
              cv_RMSE = mean(RMSE),  # get RMSE for each model (all folds)
              .groups = "drop") |>   # drop grouping for result
    left_join(wins, by = ".model") |>  # meld wins, MASE, & RMSE of each model
    mutate(origins_won = coalesce(origins_won,0L)) |>  # first non-missing value 
    arrange(cv_MASE)  # sort by MASE
  
  # > Measure 2 : Which models are consistently better?
  colorfunc_benchmark <- colorRampPalette(  # benchmark models: yellow -> orange
    c("gold", "orange", "sienna2"))  # (4 total)
  colorfunc_ETS <- colorRampPalette(  # ETS models: green -> blue
    c("forestgreen", "springgreen2", "turquoise", "deepskyblue2", "dodgerblue4"))  # (7 total)
  colorfunc_decomposition <- colorRampPalette(  # decomp models: pink -> purple
    c("pink2", "hotpink1", "violetred3", "darkmagenta", "purple4"))  # (6 total)
  model_colors <- c(  # ordered color pallet 
      "firebrick3",                 # ARIMA
      colorfunc_benchmark(4)[1],    # drift (benchmarks)
      colorfunc_ETS(7),             # ETS models
      colorfunc_benchmark(4)[2:4],  # mean, naïve, snaïve (benchmarks)
      colorfunc_decomposition(6)    # decomposition models
  )
  consistency_plot <- cv_origin |>  # RETURNED
    ggplot(aes(as.Date(origin), MASE, colour = .model, group = .model)) +
    geom_line() + 
    geom_point() +
    labs(title = region,
         subtitle = "Cross-Validation MASE At Each Forecast Origin",
         x = "Forecast Origin", 
         color = NULL) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = model_colors) +
    theme_bw()
  
  # > Measure 3 : Ljung-Box Test
  lb <- augment(fit_candidates(region_train)) |>  # use fitted original training set (not CV set)
    features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 24) |>
    mutate(passes = lb_pvalue > 0.05) |>
    arrange(desc(lb_pvalue))
  selection_info <- wins_and_measures |>  # RETURNED
    left_join(lb |> select(.model, lb_pvalue, passes), by = ".model") |>  # adds LB to accuracy info
    arrange(cv_MASE)
  
  # select the top model based on CV
  chosen_model <- selection_info |>  # RETURNED
    filter(passes) |>  # only models that pass Ljung-Box test
    slice(1) |>  # ordered by MASE, so 1st model has lowest MASE
    pull(.model)  # retrieve the model name
  
  
  # RETURNED
  return ( list(
    "consistency" = consistency_plot,  # model consistency plot
    "accuracy" = selection_info,       # CV accuracy measures and LB test results
    "chosen" = chosen_model )          # model with lowest MASE that also passes LB test
  )
}


# function to create model diagnostics for a given region and set of models
model_diagnostics <- function(region, models){
  
  # *original* training set for <region>
  region_train <- train5 |>  # original time series (no folds)
    filter(RegionName == region) |> 
    dplyr::select(-1)  # remove RegionName column
  # fit models on *original* training data
  region_OGtrain_fits <- fit_candidates(region_train)
  
  # > Measure 4 : Model Diagnostics (last resort)
  for (m in models) {  # go through all models
    print(region_OGtrain_fits |>  # use fitted original training set (not CV set)
            dplyr::select(all_of(m)) |>  # select data fitted to model m
            gg_tsresiduals() +  # time series diagnostic plots
            labs(title = m,
                 subtitle = region) +
            theme_bw())
  }
  
} 
```

### Dallas, TX

```{r}
# preform CV on Dallas, TX training data for all potential models
TX_CV_output <- regionCV("Dallas, TX") 

# extract CV results
TX_consistency_plot <- TX_CV_output$consistency  # consistency plot
TX_accuracy <- TX_CV_output$accuracy             # CV accuracy measures and LB test results
TX_chosen_model <- TX_CV_output$chosen           # model with lowest MASE that also passes LB test

# display results
kable(TX_accuracy, digits = 2)  # model accuracy measures (table)
TX_consistency_plot  # model performance across origins (plot)

# look at diagnostics of close models
TX_close_models <- c("ARIMA(auto)", 
                     "STL(annual, no trend) + ETS(A,Ad,N)", 
                     "STL(annual, no trend) + ETS(M,Ad,N)")
model_diagnostics("Dallas, TX", TX_close_models)

# determine Dallas, TX top model
# > we agree with the auto-selected top model (ARIMA(auto)) because it has the 
#   lowest MASE (by ~0.4), passes LB, has the lowest RMSE by a good bit, and 
#   consistently has the lowest MASE across origins
top_region_models <- c(top_region_models, TX_chosen_model)  # ARIMA(auto)
```

# Determine Overall Best Model (Top Performing Across All Regions)

```{r}
# make a list of each region's CV accuracy measures
region_accuracy <- list(`Dallas, TX` = TX_accuracy, 
                        `Denver, CO` = CO_accuracy, 
                        `Detroit, MI` = MI_accuracy, 
                        `Los Angeles, CA` = CA_accuracy, 
                        `New York, NY` = NY_accuracy )

# for each region, pull out the accuracy measures and display diagnostics of the top region models
for(r in attributes(region_accuracy)$names){
  # model accuracy measures
  print(
    region_accuracy[[r]] |> 
      filter(.model %in% top_region_models) |> 
      arrange(cv_MASE) |> 
      kable(caption = r)
    )
  # model diagnostics plot
  model_diagnostics(r, top_region_models) 
}

# keep track of ranks and if Ljung-Box test was passed
MASE_ranks <- data.frame(
  `ETS(M,A,A)`          = c(2, 1, 1, 2, 1),
  `ARIMA(auto)`         = c(1, 2, 3, 3, 3),
  `STL(annual) + NAIVE` = c(3, 3, 2, 1, 2)
) |> t()
LB_passed <- data.frame(
  `ETS(M,A,A)`          = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 1),
  `ARIMA(auto)`         = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  `STL(annual) + NAIVE` = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
) |> t()

# display average MASE rank and proportion of LB tests passed
kable(matrix( c(
  mean(MASE_ranks[1,]), mean(LB_passed[1,]),    # ETS(M,A,A)
  mean(MASE_ranks[2,]), mean(LB_passed[2,]),    # ARIMA(auto)
  mean(MASE_ranks[3,]), mean(LB_passed[3,])),   # STL(annual) + NAIVE
  nrow = 2, ncol = 3,
  dimnames = list(c("Average MASE Rank", "Proportion of Ljung-Box Tests Passed"),  # rows (measures)
```

# Forecast & Evaluate 

```{r}
# make forecasts for each region using the top overall model
# ??? make function for this ???
forecast_horizon <- 5*12  # how many months to forecast
```

```{r}
# fit once on the training data, no saved objects before  
stl_naive_fit <- train5 |> model(
  `STL(annual) + NAIVE` = decomposition_model(
    STL(Value ~ trend() + season(period = 12), robust = TRUE),
    NAIVE(season_adjust))
)

# forecast the test months and evaluate
stl_naive_fc <- stl_naive_fit |> forecast(new_data = test5)

stl_naive_acc <- stl_naive_fc |>
  accuracy(ts5, measures = list(RMSE = RMSE, MAE = MAE, MAPE = MAPE, MASE = MASE))

kable(stl_naive_acc, digits = 3)

stl_naive_fc |>
  autoplot(ts5 |> filter(Time >= yearmonth("2021 Jan")), level = 95) +
  facet_wrap(~RegionName, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  theme_bw()


```

# Refit series on all data and forecast
```{r}
# refit 
stl_Naive_full <- ts5 |> dplyr::select(-Date) |> model(
  `STL(annual) + NAIVE` = decomposition_model(
    STL(Value ~ trend() + season(period = 12), robust = TRUE),
    NAIVE(season_adjust))
)

# forecast 5 years (60 months)
futrue_fc <- stl_Naive_full |> forecast(h = forecast_horizon)


futrue_fc |>
  autoplot(ts5 |> filter(Time >= yearmonth("2021 Jan")), level = 95) +
  facet_wrap(~RegionName, scale = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "STL(annual) + NAIVE: 5-Year Forecast",
       x = "Time (Month)", y = "Median Price")
```
